source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

chapters.tsw_alignment_reason: The pinned SBLGNT main text contains public verse 24 and omits the movable doxology numbered 25–27; TSW omits 24 and prints the doxology at 25–27. No non-equivalent comparator text is silently aligned.

verses.rationale: Keeps Phoebe's kinship and named church ministry.
verses.before: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, a deacon of the church in Cenchreae.
verses.after: I commend to you our sister Phoebe, who is also a deacon of the church in Cenchreae.
verses.tsw_comparator: I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is also a servant of the church in Cenchreae,

verses.rationale: Preserves welcome, practical assistance, and Phoebe's patronage.
verses.before: Welcome her in the Lord in a way worthy of the holy ones, and help her in whatever matter she may need from you, because she has been a benefactor of many people, including me.
verses.after: Welcome her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matter she may need from you, for she has been a benefactor of many people, including me.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the holy ones, and assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you, for she herself has been a benefactor of many, including myself.

verses.rationale: Keeps Prisca first and names both coworkers.
verses.before: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,
verses.after: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus,

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily danger and broad gratitude.
verses.before: who risked their own necks for my life. Not only I but all the Gentile churches give thanks for them.
verses.after: They risked their own necks for my life. Not only I but all the Gentile churches give thanks for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: who for my life risked their own necks, to whom not only I give thanks but also all the churches of the Gentiles;

verses.rationale: Preserves the house church and firstfruits image.
verses.before: Greet also the church in their house. Greet my beloved Epaenetus, the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.
verses.after: Greet also the church in their house. Greet my beloved Epaenetus, the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: also greet the church in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruit of Asia for Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps Mary's labor and its recipients.
verses.before: Greet Mary, who worked very hard for you.
verses.after: Greet Mary, who has worked very hard for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Mary, who has labored much for you.

verses.rationale: Retains Junia's feminine name, imprisonment, and apostolic prominence.
verses.before: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before me.
verses.after: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and fellow prisoners. They are outstanding among the apostles, and they were in Christ before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners, who are outstanding among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the personal affection and relation in the Lord.
verses.before: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
verses.after: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps both names and distinct relationships.
verses.before: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
verses.after: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.

verses.rationale: Preserves tested approval and the household group.
verses.before: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those from Aristobulus’ household.
verses.after: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those from Aristobulus's household.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Apelles, the approved in Christ. Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus.

verses.rationale: Keeps kinship and qualifies the household members.
verses.before: Greet my relative Herodion. Greet those from Narcissus’ household who are in the Lord.
verses.after: Greet my relative Herodion. Greet those from Narcissus's household who are in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Retains all three women and the intensified labor of Persis.
verses.before: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who work hard in the Lord. Greet the beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
verses.after: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who work hard in the Lord. Greet the beloved Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis the beloved, who has labored much in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves chosen status and Paul's familial extension.
verses.before: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
verses.after: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother, who has been a mother to me as well.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

verses.rationale: Keeps every name and renders the mixed community inclusively.
verses.before: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers and sisters with them.
verses.after: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers and sisters with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers with them.

verses.rationale: Preserves every named person and the surrounding holy community.
verses.before: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all the holy ones with them.
verses.after: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas, and all the saints with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the holy ones with them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the embodied greeting and all the churches.
verses.before: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
verses.after: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the warning's objects, standard, and response.
verses.before: I urge you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who cause divisions and put obstacles in the way contrary to the teaching you learned. Turn away from them.
verses.after: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, to watch out for those who cause divisions and create obstacles contrary to the teaching you learned. Turn away from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I urge you, brothers, to watch out for those who cause divisions and obstacles contrary to the teaching which you learned, and turn away from them.

verses.rationale: Retains the belly idiom's appetite sense and the method of deception.
verses.before: For such people do not serve our Lord Christ but their own appetites, and through smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of unsuspecting people.
verses.after: For such people do not serve our Lord Christ but their own appetites, and through smooth talk and flattery they deceive the hearts of unsuspecting people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For such ones do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own belly, and by smooth speech and flattery they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.

verses.rationale: Keeps public obedience, joy, wisdom, and innocence.
verses.before: Your obedience has become known to everyone, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
verses.after: Your obedience has become known to everyone, so I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about what is good and innocent about what is evil.
verses.tsw_comparator: For your obedience has become known to all; therefore I rejoice over you, but I want you to be wise as to what is good and innocent as to what is evil.

verses.rationale: Preserves the peace/crushing tension and the pinned Christ reading.
verses.before: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.after: The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.

verses.rationale: Retains every name and distinguishes coworker from relatives.
verses.before: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
verses.after: Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
verses.tsw_comparator: Timothy my fellow worker greets you, and Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

verses.rationale: Keeps the scribe's first-person identification.
verses.before: I, Tertius, the one who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
verses.after: I, Tertius, who wrote down this letter, greet you in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, Tertius, who wrote this letter, greet you in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves hospitality, civic office, and all named greeters.
verses.before: Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, along with our brother Quartus.
verses.after: Gaius, who is host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, along with our brother Quartus.
verses.tsw_comparator: Gaius, host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, and Quartus the brother.

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned main-text benediction and its inclusive scope.
verses.before: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
verses.after: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.
verses.tsw_comparator_reason: The pinned SBLGNT main text contains public verse 24 and omits the movable doxology numbered 25–27; TSW omits 24 and prints the doxology at 25–27. No non-equivalent comparator text is silently aligned.
